about.description: What Wathiq does, how the parts fit together, and why each piece was chosen over its alternative.

twoLayers.title: Two layers, one identifier
twoLayers.body: Orkes Conductor runs the business process; LangGraph runs the AI reasoning inside one agent task. The Conductor workflow id is the LangGraph thread id, so a single identifier ties the process, the agent run and the audit trail together.

assurance.title: Assurance before automation
assurance.body: Every extracted value carries a calibrated confidence and a source region. Cases pass straight through only when the evidence supports it; everything else interrupts for a human at a mandatory or dynamic review point.

configuration.title: Configuration, not code
configuration.body: A new document type is a schema, a prompt version, cross-field rules and a golden set. Demo and Azure modes run the same code paths behind a provider interface.

about.architectureDescription: The same diagrams the backend ships, rendered live from Mermaid source.
about.serviceStatusDescription: Live health of each dependency in this deployment.
about.demoBody: Demo mode: a deterministic fake model, demo OCR, a simulated core banking system and synthetic data. The demo runs fully offline, so it cannot fail because of a network or a quota.
about.azureBody: Azure mode: Azure AI Foundry, Document Intelligence, Content Safety and AI Search are live. Only the providers behind the interfaces change — the application code is identical.

assurance.canWriteHint: This server can change a system of record. Only the posting step may call it, and only after a human approved.
assurance.readOnlyHint: Read-only: this server exposes no tool that changes anything.
assurance.allowedNodes: Graph nodes allowed to call it
assurance.namedCheckHint: A named check written in Python. A rule pack refers to it by name; adding a new kind of check is code, adding a rule is configuration.
assurance.intro: Everything on this page is read from the code that runs: the guardrails that are installed, the weights the confidence is built from, the tools each part of the agent is allowed to call, and the rule files on disk. It cannot describe a system we are not running.
assurance.guardrailsHeading: Guardrails · run on every document before anything reads it
assurance.confidenceHeading: Confidence · every field’s score is built from these five signals
assurance.calibrationLead: The weighted total is the raw score. It is then mapped through the calibration curve:
assurance.calibrationNotFitted: not fitted yet, so raw scores are shown as raw.
assurance.calibrationTail: A signal that has not been measured yet is left out and the rest are re-weighted, so a field is never punished for a check that has not run.
assurance.toolServersHeading: MCP tool servers · least privilege, one process each
assurance.toolServersNote: The investigator is given the registry, the screening list and the read-only document store. It has no address for core banking, and the broker in the API refuses the call even if it had one. That is two independent locks on the only server that can write.
assurance.rulePacksHeading: Rule packs · versioned YAML, one file per document type
assurance.namedChecksNote: Named checks registered in code: {{checks}}. A rule pack may refer to one by name; everything else is an expression, which is why adding a document type is a configuration change.
assurance.policyHeading: Policy pack · what findings cite, indexed for retrieval
assurance.policyNote: Synthetic policies written for this demonstration — not real bank policy. Indexed with: {{embedder}}. A rule that names its section quotes that section directly; a finding with no citation gets the nearest section by vector search, or no quote at all rather than a misleading one.

azure.intro: Each Azure service is switched on by its own endpoint, not by the mode alone. A service with no endpoint is not an error: the demo implementation keeps running, and this screen names it. A service that is configured and then fails is a different thing again — it raises, rather than quietly falling back, so a case is never scored by something nobody chose.
azure.authBody: On AKS this resolves to a workload identity: the pod exchanges its Kubernetes service-account token for an Entra token. No key for any Azure service is stored in the image, in a manifest or in the repository. The only two secrets that exist are the database password and the JWT signing key, and both are mounted from Key Vault.
azure.searchNote: Azure AI Search is deliberately not deployed. The free tier in this subscription belongs to another system, and a paid Basic service would replace a pgvector retriever that already returns real policy citations. The adapter is written and tested; it is not paid for.
azure.simulatedNote: Core banking, the company registry and the sanctions list remain simulated in every mode. They are MCP tool servers with synthetic data, and the Integrations tab says so. Azure mode changes how documents are read and reasoned about — not what they are checked against.

documentTypes.emptyDescription: A document type is a schema, a prompt, a rule set and a golden set — nothing in the engine changes when one is added.
documentTypes.intro: Adding a document type is configuration only: schema, prompt, cross-field rules and a golden set. The extraction engine does not change.

integrations.intro: Honest labels: Connected means a real external system answers. Simulated means the behaviour is reproduced locally and nothing leaves this machine. Demo means synthetic data stands in for a real feed.

mode.demoBody: Everything runs locally: a deterministic fake model, demo OCR, a simulated core banking system and synthetic data. Nothing is sent to an external service, so the demo cannot break because of a network or quota problem.
mode.azureBody: Azure AI Foundry, Document Intelligence, Content Safety and AI Search are in use with the keys from the environment. The same code paths run in both modes — only the provider behind the interface changes.
mode.configOnly: The mode is configuration only. Switching it does not change a line of application code.
mode.flagsDescription: What this build has switched on.

users.adminsOnlyDescription: User administration is restricted to the admin role. The API refuses this call for other roles as well.
users.caption: Users and roles

process.workflowRegistered: The workflow definition in this repository is registered on the server.
process.workflowNotRegistered: The workflow is not registered yet. A worker registers it when it starts.
process.writesExternallyHint: The only step that changes something outside Wathiq. It refuses without an approval and carries an idempotency key.
process.onlyOnRoute: only when a human is asked
process.loadError: The process layer could not be read
process.twoLayers: Conductor runs the business process and can wait days for a person. LangGraph runs the AI reasoning inside one of its tasks. The Conductor workflow id is the LangGraph thread id, so a single identifier ties the process, the reasoning and the audit trail together.
process.engineRecorded: Each case records which engine ran it, so a case processed by the fallback can never be mistaken for one that went through Conductor.
process.workflowDescription: Generated from the definition in the code, so it cannot draw a process we do not run.
process.workflowAria: The Conductor workflow Wathiq runs for a KYC refresh
process.slaBody: The timer runs beside the human review, not after it. If it fires first, the review moves to the supervisor queue and the case priority is raised — the case is never decided or cancelled on a person's behalf. A review someone is already working on stays with them.
process.sweepNote: The same sweep the timer runs. It can only escalate a review that is already overdue.
process.sweepError: The check could not be run
process.sweepForbidden: Only a supervisor or an admin can run the SLA check by hand.
